messages:
alex: midday async — onboarded llama3-tinyq variant and ran the eval harness on en/es. quick smoke: spanish short dates get truncated mid-token, e.g. '12 de abr' -> '12 de a'. pushing logs shortly.

maria: can you paste a minimal repro? might be tokenizer mismatch or kv-cache warmup.

alex: here's the smallest repro i used (input -> model output):
```
input: "La fecha es 12 de abril de 2025."
output (tinyq): "La fecha es 12 de a"

note: full log attached (segmented) — truncation happens ~after byte 26 consistently.
```

dave: hmm looks like whitespace/tokenization normalization. did we change the tokenizer rounding? which tokenizer version did you use locally vs dedicated?

alex: tokenizer v2.1.3 locally. our dedicated docker image currently has v2.0.7 per the image tag. i suspect mismatch + tinyq quant edge-case.

eval-bot: regression-alert: spanish-date-truncation >= threshold (0.74% fail rate) on llm-tinyq on recent onboard run. link: https://ci/reports/1234

sophia: i'll open a tiny CR to normalize input (collapse repeated whitespace + NFKC). also we should sync tokenizer versions in the canary image. i'll add a CI job to assert tokenizer package version.

jen: quick note — quantized tinyq already shows ~0.5% drop vs baseline on date formatting across the promptset. my rec: hold canary until normalization patch lands. :eyes:

alex: blocker: need a tiny preprocessing step (strip/control whitespace, NFKC) before tokenization in the onboarder. plan for today: add preprocess patch, run unit tests, push a smoke canary, and run the eval harness.

maria: if you want i can run the KV-cache warmup + prefix caching script after deploy to reduce cold-token flakiness. ping @eng-runtime if you need a warmup window.

deploy-bot: canary-start — route 5% traffic to llm/llama3-tinyq:canary-2026-03-17 at 12:40 UTC. monitoring: latency, token-error-rate.

dave: ack. will keep an eye on rollout dashboard.

alex: thanks all — opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/llm-perf/pull/789 (preprocess + tokenizer-version assert). i'll post a follow-up when smoke passes. :rocket:
